Hi Emma - really glad the demo was useful. Quick recap and suggested next steps below.

Recap of needs:
- P95 latency target: <= 350ms
- Steady concurrency: ~8, spikes to ~60
- Need clarity on isolation / noisy neighbor risk + SOC2 evidence

Short answers up front:
- Hosted API: designed for low friction and has a strong performance profile in general. We use request-level fair queuing and dynamic routing to reduce impact of noisy tenants, and we provide token-level cost and latency analytics. That said, Hosted does not come with dedicated GPU reservations, so if you need strict latency SLO guarantees during tenant spikes, Hosted may not meet a contractual latency SLA.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (per-customer) with predictable throughput, configurable autoscaling policies, and SLA options. This is the common choice when customers need enforced isolation and per-model latency/throughput SLOs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network and compute isolation, customer-managed networking, and optional on-prem appliances. Best for regulated workloads where you control the environment.

Hi Emma - quick technical notes to add some color for the upcoming call.

Isolation & noisy-neighbor mitigations (short):
- Hosted: multi-tenant runtime with request-level isolation. We use dynamic routing, request prioritization, and per-request token limits to prevent long-running requests from starving others. We also support prefix KV caching and prioritized batching to reduce overall token execution time. Hosted cannot provide physical GPU reservations, so tail latency during extreme platform-wide events is not contractually guaranteed.
- Dedicated: provides reserved GPU nodes for your tenant only. We enforce isolation at the orchestration layer (dedicated pods/machines), separate KV caches, and configurable compute reservations. We can attach latency objectives to routes and set autoscale policies that favor latency SLOs over cost. This is the recommended path if the 350ms P95 must be contractual.
- Private VPC/on-prem: full customer-controlled networking and compute. You run the runtime in your network (we can manage control plane or hand over fully). This is best if you have strict compliance or egress requirements.

Engineering controls we use to reduce noisy-neighbor risk:
- Continuous batching tuned to your workload distribution so long-running requests don't block short ones.
- Per-customer concurrency caps at the runtime to prevent burst storms.
- Hardware + kernel-level QoS in Dedicated pools (CPU pinning, GPU partitioning where supported).
- Warm cache strategies: KV/prefix caching warmups when we do rollouts to avoid cold-cache latency spikes.

Suggested trial: we can provision a small Dedicated pool (2-4 GPUs depending on model size) for a 2-week PoC using a synthetic replay of your traffic from the spreadsheet. We'll capture P50/P95/P99 and provide a short report. I've attached a deployment_requirements.xlsx template to capture model sizes, expected qps, and sequence lengths.

Costs: I'll let Marissa follow up with ballpark pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted credits; Private has additional engineering/onboarding fees.

Vivek and I can join the tech call; Marissa, any preferred time. Emma, please share a couple of slots and we'll confirm.
